note: Salesforce Mapping provides the salesforce_mapping config entity (maps a Drupal entity type/bundle to a Salesforce object, with sync_triggers push_create/push_update/push_delete/pull_create/pull_update/pull_delete and a field_mappings array of SalesforceMappingField plugin instances), the salesforce_mapped_object content entity, and the salesforce_mapping_field plugin type (properties, properties_extended, record_type, broken). Mapping is pure config and needs no Salesforce connection, so all medium/hard cases are grounded in real salesforce_mapping config entities created/read/modified locally, verified by pure entity reads. Cleanup deletes the namespaced sfm_* mappings.

evals.prompt: In the Salesforce suite, what config entity defines the mapping between a Drupal entity and a Salesforce object, and what does it record about which events sync?
evals.expected_output: The salesforce_mapping config entity maps a drupal_entity_type/drupal_bundle to a salesforce_object_type. Its sync_triggers control which events sync: push_create/push_update/push_delete (Drupal->SF) and pull_create/pull_update/pull_delete (SF->Drupal).

evals.prompt: How are individual field mappings represented in the Salesforce Mapping module, and what are the built-in field-mapping plugin types?
evals.expected_output: Each field mapping is a SalesforceMappingField plugin instance in the mapping's field_mappings array (plugin type salesforce_mapping_field). Built-in plugins: properties and properties_extended (map a Drupal field/property to a Salesforce field), record_type (map the SF record type), and broken (placeholder for an unavailable field).

evals.prompt: In the Salesforce suite, what entity tracks the link between a specific Drupal entity and its corresponding Salesforce record (its Salesforce Id)?
evals.expected_output: The salesforce_mapped_object content entity records the link between a specific Drupal entity and its Salesforce record (SFID). It is revisioned (capped by salesforce.settings.limit_mapped_object_revisions) and created/updated by push/pull.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Salesforce mapping named sfm_known. Inspect its live configuration and state which Salesforce object type it maps to.
evals.expected_output: It maps to the Contact object: salesforce_mapping sfm_known has salesforce_object_type = Contact (mapping the Drupal user entity to Salesforce Contact).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Salesforce mapping named sfm_trig. Inspect its live configuration and state which sync triggers are enabled.
evals.expected_output: Only the push_create and push_update sync triggers are enabled on sfm_trig (all pull_* and push_delete are false), so it pushes on Drupal entity create and update.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a Salesforce mapping with machine name sfm_task that maps the Drupal user entity (bundle user) to the Salesforce Lead object. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A salesforce_mapping config entity sfm_task exists with salesforce_object_type = Lead, drupal_entity_type = user, drupal_bundle = user (created via the mapping UI or the salesforce_mapping storage).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a Salesforce mapping sfm_ttask with all sync triggers disabled. Configure it to push to Salesforce whenever the Drupal entity is created or updated (enable the push-on-create and push-on-update triggers). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: salesforce_mapping sfm_ttask has sync_triggers.push_create = true and sync_triggers.push_update = true.
